## Summary

There is a high severity vulnerability in Traefik's Compress middleware. Brotli compression, which is enabled by default and selected by any client sending `Accept-Encoding: br`, keeps several megabytes of writer state per response until the response is fully written, and this state grows with the response size. An unauthenticated attacker can keep many compressed responses in flight, for example over a single HTTP/2 connection, and exhaust the memory of the Traefik process, denying service to every route. This is the Brotli counterpart of GHSA-x5pf-cqh3-2gv8, which fixed the same issue for zstd.

Traefik v2 is not affected: it does not support Brotli compression. Traefik v3.0 to v3.6 are affected and will not receive a patch; users on these versions should upgrade to a patched v3.7 or v3.8 release.

## Patches

- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.7.20
- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.8.0
